ONE OF THE WORST SERVICES I HAVE EVER EXPERIENCED
Nov 2024 • Family
One of the WORST restaurant I've ever tried. STRONGLY NO RECOMMEND

Table for 13 guests but only 1 waitress. Her attitude was bad, no smile on her face. Our table was booked in advance, but when all the guests came in, we had to wait for another 30 minutes for being served. Booking a table for 10 guests costs 3.8 million, adding 3 more guests costs nearly 2 million. Seafood mango spring rolls, a tiny roll with only a few thin slices of mango inside, cost nearly 90k VND/piece. Prices are extremely expensive. I asked for the bill but it took almost an hour to get the bill. There was only our group last night . I asked the staff why there's no customer but she lied like this: right now there's only our tables, but around 8-9pm there will be more groups to come. In the end, our group finished eating, paid and left at around 9 but without seeing any more customers.
Overall, it's the worst restaurant I've ever tried. Never dare to recommend it to anyone else.
ONE OF THE WORST SERVICES I HAVE EVER EXPERIENCED. AND PRICE IS EXTREMELY EXPENSIVE.
STRONGLY NO RECOMMENDATION

Nice ambience with good vietnamese foods
May 2017 • Business
Came here for a company group lunch, the venue can easily fit for 40 pax. The restaurant was hidden in one of the small road, it is not easily to find the restaurant without our local staff direction. The ambience is good with french restaurant feel inside. The food serving is slow, and they only have 2 staff at the front line to attend the customers. We order 4 dishes and one hot pot, it takes us 3 hours to complete the lunch. The foods are yumilicious. According to my colleague, this place has visited mostly by tourists and foreigners. So, i guess the pricing for the food is not cheap as well. It worth a try here but i think for me, there are other better place to dine for vietnamese foods in the city.

Charming Buffet-style Resraurant
May 2017 • Friends
My wife and I recently visited Nang Ganh with a group of friends. The location is a bit tough to find, at the end of hem 115, but the space is lovely, with high ceilings, exposed brick, and a garden area that houses the buffet. There's a wide array of traditional options, from pha lau to banh hoi. The mien xao cua was a highlight. Dessert options are excellent as well, with a variety of fruits, che, and even com ruou (fermented rice balls). Highly recommended.

(Please note that this listing is not for the Ganh restaurant on Hai Ba Trung, even though many reviewers have clearly confused the two.)
